check.population: every module, boundary and change the anti-pattern's detection signals scan
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the scanned code or the enforcing rule changes
check.refusal: the enforcing check fails the gate on a new instance, so a closed decay path cannot re-enter
check.observation: the detection signals the record lists, read from source or from runtime telemetry as each signal requires
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the principle the anti-pattern conflicts with, which the enforcing check holds new code to

records.name: Big Ball of Mud
records.definition: A defect in which a system has no discernible boundaries, so any part can depend on and change any other.
records.formed_by: Allow boundaries to remain implicit, permit unrestricted dependencies, mix concerns freely, share mutable state broadly, and accumulate changes without architectural segmentation.
measured_by: share of modules without an owner

distinctFrom.reason: A god object is one object holding many responsibilities, while divergent change is the symptom of one module changing for many reasons.
A god object concentrates responsibilities in one place, while shotgun surgery scatters one responsibility across many.
A god object is a domain object that absorbs every change, while a utility dump is a generic helper module that no one owns.

records.name: God Object
records.definition: A defect in which one object accumulates unrelated responsibilities and becomes the default place for every change.
records.formed_by: Centralize unrelated responsibilities into one object, route unrelated behavior through it, accumulate state and dependencies, and make the object the default modification point.
enforced_by: class size and responsibility limits in lint

distinctFrom.reason: Concrete coupling depends on an implementation instead of an abstraction, while a middle man is a layer of indirection that adds nothing.

records.name: Concrete Coupling
records.definition: A defect in which high-level policy depends directly on concrete implementations instead of on abstractions.
records.formed_by: Let high-level policy depend directly on low-level implementations, vendor APIs, framework classes, or concrete constructors, then spread those concrete assumptions across the core.
measured_by: concrete infrastructure imports in core modules
enforced_by: import rules that forbid infrastructure in the core

records.name: Schema Drift
records.definition: A defect in which the producers, consumers and stores of one payload evolve its shape independently until its meaning diverges.
records.formed_by: Allow producers, consumers, storage models, and documentation to evolve independently without versioned schema governance, then let payload meaning diverge over time.
measured_by: schema diff failures and consumer parse errors per release

exemplar.before:
type FooApi = { id: string; label: string };
type FooDb = { id: string; name: string; extra: string };

records.name: Implicit Contract
records.definition: A defect in which a boundary's assumptions, including the shape and meaning of the data it passes, live in behavior, naming or ordering rather than in a declared contract.
records.formed_by: Encode assumptions in code behavior, naming, ordering, timing, side effects, or undocumented payload shapes instead of declaring them as explicit contracts.
measured_by: public operations without a declared schema

exemplar.before: function saveFoo(foo) { return db.insert(foo); }
exemplar.after:
interface Foo { id: FooId; name: NonEmptyString; }
function saveFoo(foo: Foo): Promise<void> { return fooStore.save(foo); }

records.name: Hardcoded Configuration
records.definition: A defect in which environment, credential or policy values are written into code instead of being supplied as configuration.
records.formed_by: Embed environment, path, credential, feature, service endpoint, or policy values directly into code, then duplicate those assumptions across runtime contexts.
measured_by: configuration literals and secrets found in source
enforced_by: a configuration schema validated at startup

exemplar.before: const client = new FooClient("https://foo.prod.example", "sk_live_abc123");
exemplar.after:
const config = FooConfigSchema.parse({ url: process.env.FOO_URL, key: process.env.FOO_KEY });
const client = new FooClient(config);

records.name: Shared Mutable State
records.definition: A defect in which writable state is shared across modules with no owner and no synchronization.
records.formed_by: Expose writable state across modules, allow multiple actors to mutate it, omit ownership and synchronization, and let behavior depend on mutation order.
measured_by: writable state reachable from more than one module

records.name: Boundary Leakage
records.definition: A defect in which internal, persistence or vendor types cross an architectural boundary.
records.formed_by: Permit internal models, infrastructure types, persistence structures, or private module APIs to cross intended architectural boundaries.

exemplar.before: app.get("/foo/:id", async (req, res) => res.json(await ormFoo.findByPk(req.params.id)));
exemplar.after: app.get("/foo/:id", async (req, res) => res.json(toFooDto(await getFoo.execute(req.params.id))));

records.name: Manual-Only Governance
records.definition: A defect in which architecture rules or security policies exist only in documents or in reviewers' memory, with no executable check, so they drift from what the system does.
records.formed_by: Encode architecture rules in documents, meetings, or reviewer memory without executable checks, metrics, or automated enforcement.
measured_by: stated rules without an executable check
enforced_by: a rule-coverage check that requires every stated rule to name its executable gate

exemplar.before: const CONVENTION = "remember to prefix every foo id with foo_";
exemplar.after: export const rule = { id: "valid-foo-id", check: (id: string) => id.startsWith("foo_") };

records.name: Opaque Runtime Behavior
records.definition: A defect in which runtime behavior emerges from hidden reflection, registration or binding that nothing reports, so the runtime's structure and state cannot be inspected.
records.formed_by: Let runtime behavior emerge from hidden reflection, implicit registration, undocumented configuration, side effects, or untraced dynamic binding.
measured_by: dynamic bindings without a manifest entry
enforced_by: a startup report that lists every binding

exemplar.before: function processFoo(foo) { doWork(foo); }

records.name: Unowned Risk
records.definition: A defect in which a risk is never identified, or is identified and has no owner, severity, mitigation or review date.
records.formed_by: Identify a risk without assigning owner, severity, mitigation, review date, acceptance status, or escalation path.
enforced_by: a risk register whose entries are validated for owner

exemplar.before: risks.push({ title: "the foo store has no backup" });
exemplar.after: risks.push({ title: "the foo store has no backup", owner: "storage team", severity: "high", mitigation: "nightly snapshot", reviewBy: "2026-12-01" });

records.name: Unobservable Failure
records.definition: A defect in which an operation can fail without leaving a log, metric, trace or error contract.
records.formed_by: Permit operations to fail without structured logs, metrics, alerts, traces, audit records, or user-visible error contracts.
enforced_by: lint rules against empty and swallowing catch blocks

exemplar.before: try { await ship(foo); } catch { }
exemplar.after: try { await ship(foo); } catch (error) { logger.error("foo.ship.failed", error); metrics.increment("foo.ship.failure"); throw new ShipFailedError(foo.id); }

records.name: Unversioned Breaking Change
records.definition: A defect in which a public contract changes incompatibly without a version, a deprecation path or a compatibility test.
records.formed_by: Change a public API, schema, event, protocol, behavior, or package contract incompatibly without version bump, deprecation path, compatibility test, or migration notice.
measured_by: breaking diffs released without a version bump
enforced_by: API and schema diff gates in the release pipeline

exemplar.before: app.get("/foo", () => ({ label: foo.name }));
exemplar.after:
app.get("/v2/foo", () => ({ name: foo.name }));
app.get("/v1/foo", () => ({ label: foo.name }));

records.name: Distributed Monolith
records.definition: A defect in which services are deployed separately but still share data, transactions and release cycles.
records.formed_by: Split deployment units without splitting data ownership, transaction boundaries, failure isolation, contracts, or autonomous release capability.

records.name: Shotgun Surgery
records.definition: A defect in which one responsibility is scattered so that a single change needs edits in many files.
records.formed_by: Scatter one conceptual responsibility across many files so one change requires many coordinated edits.

exemplar.after:
const FOO_TAX_RATE = 0.2;
function taxFoo(value: number) { return value * FOO_TAX_RATE; }

records.name: Divergent Change
records.definition: A defect in which one module changes for many unrelated reasons.
records.formed_by: Place unrelated responsibilities in the same module so unrelated change reasons repeatedly modify one artifact.
measured_by: distinct reasons to change per module in the change history

records.name: Feature Envy
records.definition: A defect in which one module mostly works on another module's data instead of its own.
records.formed_by: Let one module repeatedly inspect or manipulate another module’s data instead of moving behavior to the data owner.

exemplar.before: function totalFoo(bar: Bar) { return bar.items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price * i.qty, 0); }
exemplar.after: class Bar { total(): Money { return this.items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.subtotal(), 0); } }

distinctFrom.reason: Inappropriate intimacy reads another module's internals, while a message chain navigates a chain of public references.

records.name: Inappropriate Intimacy
records.definition: A defect in which modules depend on each other's internal structure or private state.
records.formed_by: Allow modules or classes to rely on each other’s internals, private structure, lifecycle, or undocumented state.

exemplar.before: bar.foo._internalState.status = "ready";
exemplar.after: bar.foo.markReady();

records.name: Message Chain
records.definition: A defect in which a client navigates a chain of objects to reach the behavior it needs.
records.formed_by: Require clients to traverse a chain of objects to reach behavior or data, exposing internal object graph structure.
measured_by: member-access chain depth at call sites
enforced_by: a lint rule on member-access chain depth

exemplar.before: const city = foo.getOwner().getAddress().getCity().getName();
exemplar.after: const city = foo.ownerCityName();

records.name: Middle Man
records.definition: A defect in which a module delegates almost every call without adding behavior of its own.
records.formed_by: Insert a module that delegates almost everything without adding policy, abstraction, validation, orchestration, or simplification.
measured_by: share of methods that only delegate

exemplar.after: const fooStore: FooStore = new SqlFooStore();

distinctFrom.reason: Data clumps are one group of values traveling together unnamed, while a long parameter list is one signature with too many parameters of any kind.

records.name: Data Clumps
records.definition: A defect in which the same group of values travels together without being named as one type.
records.formed_by: Pass the same group of fields together repeatedly without naming the group as a value object or contract.

exemplar.before: function shipFoo(street: string, city: string, zip: string, country: string) {}
exemplar.after:
interface Address { street: string; city: string; zip: string; country: string; }
function shipFoo(address: Address) {}

distinctFrom.reason: Primitive obsession holds one concept in a raw primitive, while data clumps are several values that belong together as one type.
Primitive obsession is about the type of one value, while a long parameter list is about the number of parameters in one signature.

records.name: Primitive Obsession
records.definition: A defect in which domain concepts are held in raw primitives with no type or validation.
records.formed_by: Represent meaningful domain concepts as raw strings, numbers, booleans, or maps without type, validation, or behavior.
measured_by: domain concepts held in primitive types
enforced_by: type checks and a lint rule against primitive-typed domain identifiers

exemplar.before: function transfer(fooId: string, amount: number, currency: string) {}
exemplar.after:
class Money { constructor(readonly amount: number, readonly currency: Currency) {} }
function transfer(fooId: FooId, money: Money) {}

records.name: Stringly Typed Programming
records.definition: A defect in which states, types or permissions are encoded as unchecked strings.
records.formed_by: Encode behavior, types, states, permissions, or protocols as unchecked strings.
measured_by: string comparisons against values of a closed set
enforced_by: lint rules that require an enum or a discriminated union for a closed set

exemplar.before: if (foo.status === "reddy") ship(foo);
exemplar.after:
enum FooStatus { Ready, Shipped }
if (foo.status === FooStatus.Ready) ship(foo);

records.name: Boolean Trap
records.definition: A defect in which boolean parameters hide the intent of a call site.
records.formed_by: Use boolean parameters or flags that hide intent and create ambiguous call sites or combinatorial behavior.
measured_by: calls that pass more than one boolean literal
enforced_by: a lint rule against positional boolean parameters

exemplar.before: createFoo(true, false, true);
exemplar.after: createFoo({ active: true, archived: false, notify: true });

records.name: Long Parameter List
records.definition: A defect in which a signature grows so many parameters that a caller can no longer read or validate it.
records.formed_by: Grow function or constructor signatures until related inputs, optional modes, and dependencies become hard to understand or validate.
measured_by: parameters per signature above the threshold
enforced_by: a lint rule on parameter count

exemplar.before: function makeFoo(a, b, c, d, e, f, g) {}
exemplar.after:
interface MakeFooInput { a: A; b: B; c: C; d: D; e: E; f: F; g: G; }
function makeFoo(input: MakeFooInput) {}

records.name: Magic Value
records.definition: A defect in which policy, thresholds or states are written as unexplained literals.
records.formed_by: Encode policy, thresholds, status, timing, permissions, or domain rules as unexplained literals.
enforced_by: a lint rule against unnamed numeric and string literals in logic

exemplar.before: if (foo.retries > 3) fail(foo);
exemplar.after:
const MAX_FOO_RETRIES = 3;
if (foo.retries > MAX_FOO_RETRIES) fail(foo);

records.name: Speculative Generality
records.definition: A defect in which abstractions are built for variation that has no evidence of arriving.
records.formed_by: Build abstractions, extension points, layers, or configuration for variation that has no evidence of existing or near-term need.

exemplar.before: abstract class AbstractFooProviderFactoryBase<T> { abstract create(): T; }
exemplar.after: function createFoo(input: CreateFooInput): Foo { return Foo.create(input); }

distinctFrom.reason: Premature abstraction extracts shared code too early, while zombie code leaves dead code in place.

records.name: Premature Abstraction
records.definition: A defect in which a shared abstraction is extracted before its variation is understood, so it fits no caller well.
records.formed_by: Extract a shared abstraction before variation is understood, causing the abstraction to fit no use case well.
measured_by: flags and overrides per shared abstraction
enforced_by: design review against evidence of recurrence

exemplar.before:
interface FooStrategy { run(): void; }
class OnlyFooStrategy implements FooStrategy { run() {} }
exemplar.after: function runFoo() {}

distinctFrom.reason: Over-abstraction is the state of having more layers than variation, while speculative generality is the cause, building for variation not yet seen.

records.name: Over-Abstraction
records.definition: A defect in which layers, interfaces and factories outnumber the variation they serve.
records.formed_by: Add too many interfaces, layers, factories, adapters, or generic types relative to actual variability.

exemplar.before: const foo = fooFactoryProvider.getFactory().createBuilder().build();
exemplar.after: const foo = Foo.create(input);

records.name: Golden Hammer
records.definition: A defect in which one familiar solution is applied to problems regardless of fit.
records.formed_by: Apply a familiar pattern, framework, architecture style, or technology to problems regardless of fit.
enforced_by: decision records that require alternatives and the forces they answer

exemplar.before: const config = parseFooConfig(runRegexOverEverything(rawYaml));
exemplar.after: const config = FooConfigSchema.parse(yaml.load(rawYaml));

distinctFrom.reason: A cargo cult copies a pattern's shape without its forces, while a golden hammer applies one familiar solution to every problem.

records.name: Pattern Cargo Cult
records.definition: A defect in which a pattern's name and shape are copied without the forces, contracts and checks that make it work.
records.formed_by: Copy named patterns or architecture styles without implementing their required forces, contracts, constraints, or validation gates.
measured_by: patterns missing their required boundary rules or contracts
enforced_by: architecture tests that check each named pattern's required contracts

exemplar.before: class FooSingletonFactoryObserverProxy {}
exemplar.after: class FooService { constructor(private readonly store: FooStore) {} }

distinctFrom.reason: Lava flow is obsolete code kept too long, while premature abstraction is shared code extracted too early.
Lava flow is code that may still run and whose purpose nobody records, while zombie code is unreachable or disabled.

records.name: Lava Flow
records.definition: A defect in which obsolete or half-migrated code survives because nothing records whether it is still needed.
records.formed_by: Preserve obsolete, half-migrated, or unexplained code paths because no record says whether they are still needed.
measured_by: code paths with no runtime hits
deprecated code past its removal date

exemplar.after: function saveFoo(foo: Foo) { return fooStore.save(foo); }

records.name: Zombie Code
records.definition: A defect in which unreachable or disabled code stays in the system and misleads the developer and the model.
records.formed_by: Leave unreachable, unused, or disabled code in the system where it keeps misleading the developer and the model, and can be reactivated by accident.
enforced_by: unused-export and unreachable-code checks in the build

exemplar.after: function computeFoo() {}

records.name: Temporal Coupling
records.definition: A defect in which operations must be called in an undocumented order to work.
records.formed_by: Require operations to be called in a specific undocumented order for correctness.
measured_by: operations that fail when called out of order
enforced_by: types or constructors that only produce valid states

exemplar.after: const foo = Foo.start(config);

distinctFrom.reason: A hidden side effect is a query that writes, while action at a distance is one part changing behavior elsewhere through globals or listeners.

records.name: Hidden Side Effect
records.definition: A defect in which an operation that looks like a query mutates state or performs I/O that its name and signature do not show.
records.formed_by: Make an operation appear like a query or pure function while it mutates state, performs I/O, emits events, or changes global context.

exemplar.before: function getFoo(id: FooId) { audit.log(id); return fooStore.find(id); }
exemplar.after:
function getFoo(id: FooId) { return fooStore.find(id); }
function auditFooAccess(id: FooId) { audit.log(id); }

records.name: Action at a Distance
records.definition: A defect in which one part of the system changes behavior elsewhere through globals, patches or implicit listeners.
records.formed_by: Let one part of the system change behavior far away through globals, monkey patches, shared registries, ambient context, or implicit event listeners.
measured_by: global mutations and implicit listener registrations
enforced_by: lint rules against global mutation and monkey patching

exemplar.before:
globalThis.fooFlag = true;
function runFoo() { if (globalThis.fooFlag) go(); }
exemplar.after: function runFoo(options: { enabled: boolean }) { if (options.enabled) go(); }

records.name: Ambient Context
records.definition: A defect in which request, tenant or user state is read from implicit global context.
records.formed_by: Read user, tenant, locale, transaction, permissions, or request state from implicit global context instead of explicit parameters or scoped context objects.
measured_by: global context reads outside infrastructure code
enforced_by: lint rules against global context reads in business logic

exemplar.before: function saveFoo(foo) { return CurrentTenant.get().db.save(foo); }
exemplar.after: function saveFoo(foo: Foo, tenant: Tenant) { return tenant.db.save(foo); }

records.name: Inconsistent Error Model
records.definition: A defect in which one class of failure is reported through several incompatible shapes.
records.formed_by: Mix exceptions, nulls, booleans, strings, partial objects, console logging, and silent failure for the same error class.
measured_by: distinct error shapes per error class
enforced_by: a typed error contract held by the type checker

records.name: Exception Control Flow
records.definition: A defect in which exceptions carry expected branching or normal absence.
records.formed_by: Use exceptions for expected branching, normal absence, validation alternatives, or loop control.
enforced_by: lint rules against catch blocks that choose the normal path

exemplar.after:
const foo = await fooStore.find(id);
return foo ?? fooStore.create(id);

records.name: Null Semantics Drift
records.definition: A defect in which null, empty, zero and missing are used interchangeably for one field.
records.formed_by: Use null, undefined, empty string, zero, false, missing field, and empty collection interchangeably.
measured_by: fields with more than one representation of absence

exemplar.before:
const foo = find(id);
if (foo) use(foo);
exemplar.after:
const foo = find(id) ?? Foo.none();
foo.use();

records.name: Anemic Domain Model
records.definition: A defect in which domain objects hold data only, while their rules live in services and handlers.
records.formed_by: Store domain data in passive objects while business rules live in services, controllers, handlers, or scripts.
enforced_by: architecture tests that locate domain rules

exemplar.before:
class Foo { status: string; }
function shipFoo(foo: Foo) { if (foo.status === "ready") foo.status = "shipped"; }

records.name: Transaction Script Sprawl
records.definition: A defect in which business processes are procedural scripts that coordinate validation, persistence and decisions directly.
records.formed_by: Encode business processes as procedural scripts that directly coordinate validation, persistence, external calls, and domain decisions.

distinctFrom.reason: A fat controller puts business logic in the request handler, while transaction script sprawl writes business processes as procedural scripts wherever they live.

records.name: Fat Controller
records.definition: A defect in which controllers hold validation, business rules, persistence and response formatting.
records.formed_by: Put validation, business rules, persistence orchestration, mapping, authorization, and response formatting in the controller layer.
enforced_by: layer rules that keep domain logic out of controllers

records.name: Repository Dump
records.definition: A defect in which a repository accumulates business queries, policy and orchestration until it is a second service layer.
records.formed_by: Place business-specific querying, orchestration, mapping, caching, validation, and policy into a repository until it becomes a second service layer.

exemplar.before: class FooRepository { findActiveFoosForBarInRegionSortedByBaz() {} }
exemplar.after: class FooRepository { find(spec: FooSpecification): Foo[] { return this.query(spec.toQuery()); } }

distinctFrom.reason: A utility dump gathers unrelated helpers in one module, while shotgun surgery spreads one responsibility across many files.

records.name: Utility Dump
records.definition: A defect in which unrelated helpers accumulate in a generic utility module that no one owns.
records.formed_by: Accumulate unrelated helper functions in generic utility modules without ownership, cohesion, or domain language.
enforced_by: naming rules that reject catch-all module names

exemplar.after:
export const fooFormatter = { format(foo: Foo): string {} };
export const barParser = { parse(raw: string): Bar {} };

records.name: Framework Leakage
records.definition: A defect in which framework or infrastructure types, annotations or lifecycles enter core domain logic, so business rules depend on technical specifics.
records.formed_by: Let framework classes, decorators, lifecycle assumptions, request objects, ORM entities, or infrastructure annotations enter core domain logic.
enforced_by: import rules that keep framework packages out of the core

exemplar.before: class Foo { @Column() name: string; @OneToMany() bars: Bar[]; }
exemplar.after:
class Foo { constructor(readonly name: string, readonly bars: readonly Bar[]) {} }
class FooEntity { @Column() name: string; }

records.name: Vendor Lock-In Leakage
records.definition: A defect in which an external system's or a vendor's APIs, errors and models spread through application and domain code, so their changes ripple across it.
records.formed_by: Spread vendor-specific APIs, models, exceptions, identifiers, or configuration throughout application and domain code.
enforced_by: import rules that confine vendor packages to adapters

exemplar.before:
import { BlobStore } from "acme-blob-sdk";
function saveFoo(foo) { return new BlobStore().putObject(foo); }
exemplar.after:
interface FooBlobStore { put(foo: Foo): Promise<void>; }
function saveFoo(foo: Foo, store: FooBlobStore) { return store.put(foo); }

distinctFrom.reason: A circular dependency is a cycle in the dependency graph, while inappropriate intimacy is a dependency on another module's internals, with or without a cycle.
A circular dependency is a cycle between modules, while a message chain is a client walking a chain of objects.

records.name: Circular Dependency
records.definition: A defect in which modules depend on each other, directly or through others, so none can change alone.
records.formed_by: Allow modules to depend on each other directly or indirectly until no module can change, test, deploy, or initialize independently.
enforced_by: a dependency-cycle check in the build

records.name: Cyclic Deployment Dependency
records.definition: A defect in which services must deploy in lockstep because each depends on the other's current version.
records.formed_by: Require two or more services or packages to deploy in lockstep because each depends on the other’s current behavior.

exemplar.before:
fooService.callsAtStartup(barService);
barService.callsAtStartup(fooService);
exemplar.after:
fooService.publishes(fooReady);
barService.subscribes(fooReady);

records.name: Synchronous Chain Trap
records.definition: A defect in which one request depends on a deep chain of blocking synchronous remote calls, so one slow link stalls the whole request.
records.formed_by: Build deep request-time chains across services or modules, making latency, availability, and failure behavior multiplicative.
measured_by: synchronous call depth per request path

exemplar.after: const [foo, bar, baz] = await Promise.all([a(), b(), c()]);

records.name: Chatty Interface
records.definition: A defect in which one operation needs many small remote calls.
records.formed_by: Require many small remote calls to complete one user or business operation.
enforced_by: performance tests that bound call counts

exemplar.before:
const results = [];
for (const id of fooIds) results.push(await fooApi.get(id));
exemplar.after: const results = await fooApi.getMany(fooIds);

records.name: N Plus One Query
records.definition: A defect in which a collection is fetched and then one further query is issued per item.
records.formed_by: Fetch a collection, then issue one query or remote call per item rather than fetching required related data intentionally.
measured_by: queries per request as the row count grows

exemplar.before:
const foos = await fooStore.all();
for (const foo of foos) foo.bar = await barStore.find(foo.barId);
exemplar.after:
const foos = await fooStore.all();
const bars = await barStore.findMany(foos.map(f => f.barId));

records.name: Cache Poisoning by Design
records.definition: A defect in which a cache key omits an input the entry depends on, so one request is served another's result.
records.formed_by: Cache data without key correctness, tenant isolation, authorization context, invalidation, or schema version, or key the entry by time or lifetime alone.
enforced_by: tests that vary tenant and version

exemplar.before: fooCache.set(request.path, response);

records.name: Retry Storm
records.definition: A defect in which clients retry a failing dependency so aggressively that the retries prolong the failure.
records.formed_by: Allow many clients or workers to retry failed dependencies aggressively and synchronously, increasing pressure on the failing system.
measured_by: retry share of load during incidents
enforced_by: a resilience policy that requires bounded retries with backoff and jitter

exemplar.before: while (true) { try { return await call(); } catch { } }
exemplar.after: return retry(call, { attempts: 5, backoff: exponentialJitter(), giveUp: dlq });

records.name: Timeout Omission
records.definition: A defect in which calls to external systems carry no timeout, cancellation or deadline, so a caller can wait for ever on work that never completes.
records.formed_by: Call external systems without explicit timeouts, cancellation, or deadline propagation.
enforced_by: a lint rule that requires a timeout on outbound calls

exemplar.before: const foo = await fetch(fooUrl);
exemplar.after: const foo = await fetch(fooUrl, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });

records.name: Missing Backpressure
records.definition: A defect in which a system accepts work faster than it can process it, with no limit or shedding.
records.formed_by: Accept work faster than the system can process it without queue limits, admission control, rate limits, or shedding.
measured_by: queue depth and memory growth under load
enforced_by: checks that every queue is configured with a bound

exemplar.before: stream.on("data", d => queue.push(process(d)));
exemplar.after: stream.pipe(new BoundedFooProcessor({ highWaterMark: 100 }));

records.name: Silent Data Corruption
records.definition: A defect in which invalid data is accepted, transformed or stored without any check noticing.
records.formed_by: Accept, transform, or persist invalid data without validation, checksums, invariants, reconciliation, or audit.

exemplar.before:
const total = Number(a) + Number(b);
save(total);
exemplar.after:
const total = Money.add(Money.parse(a), Money.parse(b));
save(total);

records.name: Lost Update
records.definition: A defect in which concurrent writers overwrite each other's changes without a version check.
records.formed_by: Allow concurrent writers to overwrite each other without version checks, locks, compare-and-swap, or transaction isolation.
measured_by: concurrent update conflicts found in tests

exemplar.after: await fooStore.update(id, { count: increment(1) }, { expectedVersion: foo.version });

records.name: Dual Write
records.definition: A defect in which related state is written to two systems with no atomicity or compensation.
records.formed_by: Write related state to two systems without atomicity, outbox, saga, reconciliation, or compensation.
measured_by: writes to two systems outside one transaction or outbox

exemplar.before:
await db.save(foo);
await searchIndex.add(foo);
exemplar.after:
await db.save(foo);
await outbox.append(fooCreatedEvent(foo));

records.name: Read-Your-Writes Violation
records.definition: A defect in which a writer reads back a stale copy of what it has just written.
records.formed_by: Let users or processes perform a write and then read from a stale replica, cache, projection, or eventually consistent view without explicit consistency contract.
enforced_by: consistency-contract tests that read after a write

exemplar.before:
await primaryDb.write(foo);
const view = await replicaDb.read(foo.id);
exemplar.after:
await primaryDb.write(foo);
const view = await readAfterWrite(foo.id, { consistency: "read-your-writes" });

records.name: Security Theater
records.definition: A defect in which visible security controls leave the real threat unreduced, or can be bypassed.
records.formed_by: Add visible security controls that do not reduce the actual threat model or can be bypassed by alternate paths.
measured_by: controls not linked to a threat

exemplar.before: if (password.length > 0) grantFooAccess(user);

records.name: Authorization Scattering
records.definition: A defect in which authorization checks are spread across layers with no central policy.
records.formed_by: Spread authorization checks across controllers, services, repositories, UI, and ad hoc conditionals without a central policy model.
enforced_by: a policy engine, with authorization tests per endpoint

exemplar.before:
if (user.role === "admin") deleteFoo();
if (user.role === "admin" || user.id === foo.owner) editFoo();
exemplar.after:
if (policy.can(user, "delete", foo)) deleteFoo();
if (policy.can(user, "edit", foo)) editFoo();

records.name: Secret Sprawl
records.definition: A defect in which credentials and keys are stored across code, logs and configuration.
records.formed_by: Store credentials, tokens, keys, certificates, or sensitive configuration across code, config files, logs, tickets, and local environments.
measured_by: secrets found in source and logs

exemplar.before:
const key = "sk_live_abc123";
const dbPass = "hunter2";
exemplar.after:
const key = await secrets.get("foo.api.key");
const dbPass = await secrets.get("foo.db.password");

records.name: Personal Data Oversharing
records.definition: A defect in which more personal data is collected, kept, logged or exposed than the declared purpose needs.
records.formed_by: Collect, store, log, transmit, or expose more personal data than needed for the declared purpose.
measured_by: personal-data fields in logs and exports

exemplar.before: logger.info("created foo", { email: user.email, ssn: user.ssn });
exemplar.after: logger.info("created foo", { userId: user.id });

records.name: Observability Noise
records.definition: A defect in which logs, metrics and alerts are too many and too low in signal to act on.
records.formed_by: Emit excessive, low-signal logs, metrics, traces, or alerts without severity, ownership, cardinality control, or actionability.

exemplar.before:
logger.info("entering loop");
for (const f of foos) logger.info("iter", f);
exemplar.after: logger.info("foo.batch.processed", { count: foos.length, durationMs });

records.name: Log-as-Control-Flow
records.definition: A defect in which a failure is logged as though logging handled it, and execution continues.
records.formed_by: Log errors or warnings as if logging itself handles the failure, while the system continues without recovery, propagation, or safe fallback.
measured_by: catch blocks that log and continue
enforced_by: a lint rule against catch blocks that only log

exemplar.before:
try { await chargeFoo(foo); } catch (error) { logger.error("foo.charge.failed", error); }
shipFoo(foo);

records.name: Manual Runbook Dependency
records.definition: A defect in which repeatable operational steps, such as detecting a failure and recovering from it, are performed by hand during incidents and deploys, so recovery waits on a person.
records.formed_by: Perform by hand the repeatable operational actions during incidents, deploys, migrations, or recovery.
enforced_by: operations review of manual steps repeated across incidents

exemplar.before: const RUNBOOK = "on failure, ssh in and run restart-foo.sh";
exemplar.after: health.onUnhealthy(() => orchestrator.restart("foo"));

records.name: Big-Bang Release
records.definition: A defect in which a large, irreversible change reaches every user at once, with no staged rollout.
records.formed_by: Ship a large, irreversible, all-user change without staged rollout, feature flags, canary, rollback, or blast-radius control.
enforced_by: release gates that require a canary or a feature flag and a rollback plan

exemplar.before: deployEverything("foo", "bar", "baz");
exemplar.after: release("foo", { strategy: canary(0.1) });

records.name: Irreversible Migration
records.definition: A defect in which a schema or data change can neither run beside the old version nor be rolled back.
records.formed_by: Apply schema, data, or infrastructure changes that cannot safely run alongside old versions or be rolled back.
measured_by: migrations without a down step or a compatible phase

exemplar.before: await db.exec("ALTER TABLE foo DROP COLUMN legacy_name");
exemplar.after: await migrate({ up: addFooName, down: restoreFooName });

distinctFrom.reason: Frozen architecture fixes decisions too early, while lava flow keeps obsolete code too long.
Frozen architecture fixes system-level decisions early, while premature abstraction extracts one shared abstraction early.
Frozen architecture is a decision made too early, while zombie code is dead code left behind.

records.name: Big-Upfront Frozen Architecture
records.definition: A defect in which major architectural decisions are fixed before the forces they answer are known.
records.formed_by: Lock in major architectural decisions before validating domain forces, quality attributes, operational realities, and change vectors.

exemplar.before: const ARCHITECTURE = designAllModulesForNextFiveYears();
exemplar.after:
const foo = defineModule("foo", { exports: { createFoo } });
registry.add(foo);

distinctFrom.reason: An astronaut builds frameworks for needs that have not arrived, while over-abstraction adds layers beyond the variation that exists.
An astronaut builds whole frameworks and meta-models, while speculative generality is one abstraction built for variation with no evidence of arriving.

records.name: Architecture Astronaut
records.definition: A defect in which abstract frameworks, meta-models and architectural structure are built ahead of the concrete needs they should serve.
records.formed_by: Prefer abstract frameworks, taxonomies, meta-models, and generic engines over concrete user, domain, and operational needs.
measured_by: generic components with few real consumers
enforced_by: design review against real use cases

exemplar.before: class AbstractFooMetaStrategyOrchestrationEngineFactory {}
exemplar.after: class CreateFoo { execute(input: CreateFooInput): Foo {} }

records.name: Feature-Only Design
records.definition: A defect in which architecture serves immediate features while its quality attributes go unaddressed.
records.formed_by: Optimize architecture for immediate feature delivery while ignoring quality attributes such as security, operability, scalability, maintainability, and evolvability.

exemplar.before: function addFooFeature() { hack(); patch(); bypassLint(); }
exemplar.after: function addFooFeature(input: CreateFooInput) { return createFoo.execute(input); }

records.name: Test Pyramid Inversion
records.definition: A defect in which a test suite relies mainly on slow end-to-end tests, with few unit and contract tests.
records.formed_by: Rely mainly on slow, brittle end-to-end tests while unit, contract, component, and property tests are sparse.

records.name: Mock Mirage
records.definition: A defect in which tests assert calls on mocks rather than observable behavior or contracts.
records.formed_by: Overuse mocks so tests verify internal calls rather than observable behavior or contracts.
measured_by: tests that break on refactors with no change in behavior

exemplar.before: const store = { save: fn(), find: fn().returns(foo) };
exemplar.after:
const store = new InMemoryFooStore();
runFooStoreContract(store);

records.name: Flaky Test Normalization
records.definition: A defect in which intermittent test failures are accepted and rerun until they pass.
records.formed_by: Accept intermittent test failures as normal and rerun until green instead of fixing nondeterminism or isolation defects.
measured_by: quarantined tests past their fix date
enforced_by: a CI policy that fails on a retried test and tracks every quarantined one

exemplar.before: test.retry(5)("foo works sometimes", async () => { await sleep(random()); expect(await getFoo()).toBeTruthy(); });
exemplar.after: test("foo is created deterministically", async () => { const foo = await createFoo.execute(input); expect(foo.id).toBe(expectedId); });

records.name: Prompt Sprawl
records.definition: A defect in which prompts, model parameters and output schemas are scattered through code without versions or evaluation.
records.formed_by: Scatter prompts, retrieval rules, model parameters, safety instructions, and output schemas across code without versioning, evaluation, or ownership.
enforced_by: a prompt registry, with an evaluation required on every change

exemplar.before:
const a = model.run("summarize this foo: " + foo);
const b = model.run("pls summarize foo " + foo);
exemplar.after: const summary = model.run(FOO_PROMPTS.summarize({ foo }));

records.name: Ungrounded Content
records.definition: A defect in which the model produces answers or decisions without retrieved evidence or disclosed uncertainty.
records.formed_by: Generate answers, classifications, plans, or decisions without evidence retrieval, source references, confidence limits, or unsupported-claim handling.
measured_by: answers without a source where one is required
enforced_by: claim validation against the retrieved sources

exemplar.before:
const answer = await model.run(question);
return answer;

records.name: Model Version Ambiguity
records.definition: A defect in which models, prompts or indexes are used without recording their version and configuration.
records.formed_by: Use models, embeddings, prompts, or evaluation artifacts without recording version, configuration, dataset, or inference context.
measured_by: inferences logged without a model version
enforced_by: inference logging that requires a version

exemplar.before: const result = await model.run(prompt);
exemplar.after:
const result = await model.run(prompt, { model: "foo-llm-2024-06", temperature: 0 });
logger.info("foo.inference", { model: result.model });
